name: Praising.ai
oneLiner: Low-cost AI review management tool for local businesses, with review requests, AI-drafted replies and rating tracking, plus a restaurant version of its marketing.
bestFor: Independent restaurants and small local businesses that want simple review collection and AI reply drafting at a low monthly price.
features: Review requests by email and text after a visit, with automatic reminders for customers who haven't clicked
Review links and QR codes for receipts, table tents and posters, plus a kiosk mode for a counter tablet
AI-drafted replies that the owner approves before posting
One inbox for reviews from Google, Yelp, Facebook, Tripadvisor and other sites
Tracking of review volume, rating trends and reply rates, with multi-location support
Review page in Spanish, French and other languages
Visibility section with Maps ranking and AI ranking
API and webhooks for connecting other systems

pricing.text: Core $19 per location per month, Growth $29, Pro $49; a free trial and no annual contract. Vendor pages disagree on trial length (7 or 14 days) and whether a card is needed.

notes: Only vendor sources found; no named customers, press coverage or third-party reviews. Changelog (praising.ai/changelog) lists recent features (text requests, reminders, languages, kiosk mode, Visibility, API/webhooks) but has no dates, so no dated updates were recorded. The current review calls it 'built specifically for restaurants'; most of its site describes a general local-business tool with restaurant landing pages, so that framing should be softened. Its pages say it does not connect directly to OpenTable, Resy, Toast or Square. Dropped 'auto-publish for reviews above a rating you choose' (vendor pages say nothing is posted until you approve; not confirmed). Pages disagree on whether low ratings are routed to a private form, so that was left out.
